# Tools - [`jlink`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/jlink.html)

The `jlink` tool can be used to assemble and optimise a set of modules and their
dependencies into a custom (compact) runtime image. The `jlink` tool will only
package modules that are required by the application leaving out unnecessarily
modules. This will produce smaller deployment units. Furthermore, Java is not
required on the OS as this is part of the custom (compact) runtime image.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── logback-classic-1.6.3.jar
   ├── logback-core-1.6.3.jar
   ├── slf4j-api-2.0.18.jar
   └── tools-jlink.jar

   1 directory, 4 files
   ```

2. List all modules

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --list-modules
   ```

3. Create custom runtime image

   ```shell
   jlink \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules demo \
     --output './target/dist' \
     --launcher app=demo
   ```

   (*Optional*) View the created custom runtime

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name './target/dist'
   ```

   The custom image

4. Run the application

   ```shell
   ./target/dist/bin/app
   ```

   The application will run and print

   ```
   SLF4J(W): No SLF4J providers were found.
   SLF4J(W): Defaulting to no-operation (NOP) logger implementation
   SLF4J(W): See https://www.slf4j.org/codes.html#noProviders for further details.
   ```

   It looks like the logback modules are not part of the application. These are
   not required by the `demo` module.

5. Analyse the custom image

   Calculate the size of the custom image.

   ```shell
   du --summarize --human-readable './target/dist'
   ```

   The size of the custom image

   ```
   58M	./target/dist
   ```

   Print the size of the modules.

   ```shell
   du --summarize --human-readable './target/dist/lib/modules'
   ```

   The size of the modules that are part of this custom image

   ```
   29M	./target/dist/lib/modules
   ```

   This file contains all modules used by this program. Its current size is
   about 29MB.

   The `jimage` can be used to describe this file

   ```shell
   jimage info './target/dist/lib/modules'
   ```

   This will print the size together other information

   ```
    Major Version:  1
    Minor Version:  0
    Flags:          0
    Resource Count: 7919
    Table Length:   7919
    Offsets Size:   31676
    Redirects Size: 31676
    Locations Size: 152803
    Strings Size:   192653
    Index Size:     408836
   ```

   and list its contents

   ```shell
   jimage list './target/dist/lib/modules'
   ```

   This will print all modules found in the custom image

   ```
   jimage: ./target/dist/lib/modules

   Module: demo
       META-INF/MANIFEST.MF
       META-INF/maven/demo/tools-jlink/pom.properties
       META-INF/maven/demo/tools-jlink/pom.xml
       demo/Main.class
       module-info.class

   Module: java.base
       META-INF/services/java.nio.file.spi.FileSystemProvider
       com/sun/crypto/provider/AEADBufferedStream.class
   ...
   ```

   Some of the output is truncated for brevity.

   Filter the modules

   ```shell
   jimage list './target/dist/lib/modules' | grep 'Module: '
   ```

   This will print only the module names found in the custom image

   ```
   Module: demo
   Module: java.base
   Module: org.slf4j
   ```

6. Create custom runtime image (including the logback modules)

   Delete the output directory to remove any residue that may remain from the
   previous run.

   ```shell
   rm -rf './target/dist'
   ```

   Create the custom runtime image (including the logback modules).

   ```shell
   jlink \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules demo,ch.qos.logback.classic \
     --output './target/dist' \
     --launcher app=demo
   ```

   (*Optional*) View the created custom runtime

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name './target/dist'
   ```
